newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE white sugar touch weaker, awaits NY direction.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE white sugar touch weaker, awaits NY direction.

text.p: Nearby white sugar futures eased slightly in a subdued start to the week's trading on Monday as London traders awaited the New York open to gauge market sentiment after the March raws expiry.
A mixed bag of sellers, including brokers and commission houses, pushed the May whites contract lower, with the weakness partially offset by trade buying.
A limited number of crosses boosted the overall volume, which stayed on the low side at just 293 lots by 1210 GMT.
May was down 70 cents at $308.30 and August down $1.00 at $307.10.
Traders said the New York market would probably correct lower now that March had gone off the board but could still move either way and make the May/May arbitrage a focus of interest.

"The feeling is that now March is out of the way, the market will tend to come off," said one trader, noting commission house and fund stops at around 10.75 cents/lb basis May and trade stops at just over 11.00.
Technical analysts said they would maintain a bullish stance to the London whites market while a trendline dating from January remained intact.
May values were heading for a test of $312 but an initial barrier of $310 could still prove a tricky hurdle, they said.

Fresh physical news was thin on the ground, although the deliveries against March raws were an obvious talking point. The results of Bangladesh's weekend tender to buy a cargo of white sugar have yet to emerge.
Activity in Paris was exceedingly thin, with May unchanged at $308.50 and August untraded. Matif volume totalled an unimpressive 15 lots.
